wordmark.purpose: The two words "Ngó Sen" on the hero sheet; the header repeats the setting at 1.7rem. word-spacing -0.28em.

display.purpose: Title of a read page. word-spacing -0.2em.

headline.purpose: Section headings on the home page. word-spacing -0.2em.

title.purpose: Headings inside a guide or post, and post titles in lists. word-spacing -0.2em.

typed.purpose: Measured claims, system names, third-level headings in prose.

typed-output.purpose: The single line the typing run writes on the hero sheet; never wraps.

code.purpose: Commands, code blocks and inline code; wraps rather than scrolls.

lede.purpose: The one sentence under a title.

body.purpose: Running text, capped at 68ch. Emphasis is weight 600.

small.purpose: Sources, bases and notes, in muted ink.

label.purpose: Keycap legends, column heads, dates and small uppercase links. Uppercase, 0.95rem to 1.1rem.

stamp.purpose: Tested-level stamps. Uppercase; weight 500 on the bracket form.

shadows.name: key-rest
shadows.purpose: Under every live keycap, together with the 0.3em skirt.

shadows.name: key-pressed
shadows.purpose: Keycap moved down 0.22em: active, or the key being typed in the run.

shadows.name: key-current
shadows.purpose: Ribbon line along the bottom of the current page's nav key, which stays pressed.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Paper sheet on the desk: hairline edge plus a contact shadow under the bottom edge.

shadows.name: roller
shadows.purpose: The roller the hero sheet feeds out of.

shadows.name: stamp-double
shadows.purpose: Inner ring of the double-box stamp; --stamp-ground is set to the surface the stamp sits on.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: Doubles the typing field's underline on focus.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing; used for every transition.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: Transform and box-shadow on a keycap's hover and press.

motion.name: demo-key
motion.purpose: Keys in the typing run going down and fading once used.

motion.name: typing-run-key
motion.purpose: Interval between keys in the scripted typing run.

motion.name: typing-run-hold
motion.purpose: Pause on a finished phrase before the next one; the run plays three phrases once and stops.

motion.name: visitor-key-flash
motion.purpose: How long the visitor's latest key stays pressed in the row.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The typing run does not start; transitions and animations collapse to 0.01ms.

widths.name: page-sheet
widths.purpose: The single sheet of a read page.

narrative.overview:
The site is a machine you can watch typing. An enamel green body carries the keys, ivory keycaps go down when pressed, and whatever was typed or measured comes out on a sheet of paper. Before any claim is made, keystrokes turn into Vietnamese in front of the visitor. The palette is the machine's own materials: enamel, ivory caps, paper, carbon ink, and one red ribbon.

Every surface is one of three grounds, and the ground says what kind of content it holds. The enamel band carries the machine (the header, the hero, the Telex keyboard). Paper sheets carry anything typed or measured (the wordmark, the demo line, tested systems, measured results, guides, posts). The ink strip carries commands and the footer. Between them is the desk, a pale green-grey the sheets rest on.

Density is unhurried on the home page and plain on read pages: the install guide, the comparison page and blog posts are a single sheet on the desk with one text column. Both colour schemes are authored; the dark one follows the system setting and keeps the same materials, with paper lifted clear of the desk so a sheet still reads as a sheet.

Motion is one authored moment: the typing run in the hero. Everything else is a short press.
keyCharacteristics: Three grounds with fixed jobs: enamel for the machine, paper for typed or measured content, ink for commands.
Keycaps are the only button shape, and they move the way a key does.
Ribbon red is reserved for a short, fixed list of marks.
Tested levels are told apart by outline form, never by colour.
Three typefaces with fixed voices: typed, legend, body.
Commands wrap; nothing a visitor must copy scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The Ribbon Rule
rules.body: Ribbon red marks the install copy key, the caret, the "Chưa sửa" struck mark, focus and selection, and the line under the current page's nav key. Nothing else. No red headings, links, badges or decoration.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: Enamel carries the machine, paper carries what was typed or measured, the ink strip carries commands and the footer. New content picks its ground by what it is, not by which colour the page is short of.

rules.name: The Ground Decides Focus Rule
rules.body: The focus ring is a 2px outline at 3px offset in `ribbon-text` on paper and desk. On enamel it switches to `on-enamel` and on the ink strip to `on-strip`, because red on enamel green has almost no contrast.

rules.name: The Closed Word Space Rule
rules.body: A monospace word space is a full cell, and at heading sizes it reads as a gap. Xanh Mono headings set `word-spacing: -0.2em`; the wordmark sets `-0.28em`. A heading that switches to the legend font resets word-spacing to normal.

rules.name: The Typed or Measured Rule
rules.body: Xanh Mono is for what the machine produced or what was measured: names, numbers, results, commands, headings. Explanations and notes around them are Barlow.

rules.name: The Marks Stay Whole Rule
rules.body: Vietnamese stacked marks (ế, ỗ, ặ) must stay legible at every size used. Lines of large typed text keep room above and below the line box rather than clipping.

rules.name: The Skirt Rule
rules.body: A key's height is its skirt: a 0.3em bottom edge in the skirt colour. Pressing moves the cap down and shortens the shadow. Hover is a 0.08em dip, active is 0.22em, both over 120ms. Keys that are legends rather than controls (dimmed Telex keys) carry no shadow.

rules.name: The Sheets Stay Sheets Rule
rules.body: In the dark scheme paper is lifted well above the desk so the sheet edge is visible without relying on the shadow.

dos: Do choose the ground by content: enamel for the machine, paper for typed or measured content, the ink strip for commands and the footer.
Do make every button a keycap with a skirt, and let it move down when pressed (0.08em hover, 0.22em active, 120ms).
Do set Xanh Mono headings with `word-spacing: -0.2em` and the wordmark with `-0.28em`; reset it when a heading uses the legend font.
Do tell tested levels apart by stamp form (double box, single box, brackets) and put the basis for the claim next to the stamp.
Do let commands and code wrap, and give the install command a ribbon copy key wherever it appears.
Do switch the focus ring to the light text colour on enamel and on the ink strip.
Do keep stacked Vietnamese marks whole: leave room above and below large typed lines.
Do author both colour schemes, with dark paper lifted clear of the dark desk.
Do keep transitions to transform, opacity and box-shadow, between 120ms and 240ms, and keep the reduced-motion path working.
donts: Don't use ribbon red for anything outside the Ribbon Rule's list: no red headings, links, badges or decoration.
Don't carry a tested level, or any other state, by colour alone.
Don't loop the typing run or add a second authored animation; the run plays once and stops.
Don't make a command scroll sideways on a narrow screen.
Don't set running text in Xanh Mono or body paragraphs in the legend font.
Don't set Xanh Mono in bold; only regular and italic exist.
Don't draw a pictorial logo. The mark is the two words "Ngó Sen" set in Xanh Mono, always with diacritics.
Don't float surfaces with wide ambient shadows or glows; shadows are contact shadows under an edge.
